comments.text:
I agree with this, came back to re-watch the review and AMD did do an extremely poor job marketing it, but as a RTX 4080 competitor, just doesn't make sense - at today's pricing - to get an RTX 4080, even for high end buyers (sorry Steve). In my region, Australia, subtracting our 10% tax, I picked up an RX 7900 XTX, on sale, for $888 USD, and it's a solid AIB model. The cheapest RTX 4080 available was $1184 USD, these are odd numbers because I'm using today's currency conversion back to USD. In short the RX 7900 XTX was 75% the price of the RTX 4080, and it had performance advantages in games I wanted to play - absolute no brainer. Even 5 years later, there are barely any ray tracing games, sure I'll try it out for fun if a title I'm playing has it, otherwise still not a must have / factor. Lastly, Upscaling at 4K, FSR 2 vs DLSS 2, yep, DLSS is still a bit better, but it is negligible once you're at 4K, even more so using 75% render resolution, but at 4K you can get away with 50% imo in several games.
If the 6800 XT is doing what you want it to do I'd keep it as long as possible, AMD aren't really on track to release anything amazing for 3 or 4 years so, I'd try and go the distance until the 9000 or 10000 series, RDNA5 whichever that is, RDNA4 will be the same or less performance than today at lower prices, from the latest rumours I've heard of.

comments.text:
At one point this man claims that the 7900XTX is "underwhelming" due to a 4FPS difference between it and the 4080. Also claims that people looking at the 6950XT will often be "disappointed" in the 7900XTX's performance. If someone is looking at a card that was released six months prior to this 7900XTX expecting crazy 50% gains in performance...I don't know what to tell that person.  It may have happened in the past but that doesn't mean its going to happen every single time.  That would be an unrealistic expectation. Also, why would said person have bought a GPU a few months ago and then want to buy another now? That type of consumer is almost irrelevant because they are never going to be pleased.

One annoying thing about all this GPU war stuff is that Nvidia has so many game devs and such in their pocket.  As we see with some of the benchmarks, AMD cards are capable of an incredible amount, but AMD isnt good at securing these deals to work with devs AND many SDKs probably play better with Nvidia over AMD. But AMD's performance on its own is often just as good as Nvidia. Can't do much when other companies tailor their software for your competitor.

The 7900XTX has been great for me coming from a 2080. I have no brand loyalty, I just buy whatever works best for me at the time. The card actually fits in my case unlike the 4080 and I get essentially the same exact performance out of it for cheaper than the 4080. Raytracing performance is obviously way better on Nvidia, and I would like to have it. But having to buy a new case/take out my AIO and pay more money for the 4080 to experience raytracing in maybe two games of note (cyberpunk and witcher 3) isn't worth it for me at least.  All this number crunching and data can be fun to observe and think about. But in the end, unless you are staring at your FPS counter all game, you wouldn't even know if you have a 7900 or a 4080 in your computer anyway. Its practically the same thing in rasterization to the point where there is nothing to discuss other than ray tracing and TDP.

comments.text:
I don't get why you're comparing this card with the RTX 4090, it's simply ridiculous. They are not in the same league and AMD has made it clear since the beginning. The NVIDIA flagship is more than 60% more expensive, it's more like a Prosumer card, not just a gaming GPU. That also explains the better media encoding/decoding and AI capabilities. The AMD 7900 XTX is oriented more towards regular and enthusiast gamers.

Also, the AMD presentation constantly emphasized that the difference between this card and the previous gen 6950XT in 4K and RT performance was up to those percentages and it stated specifically on which games that differences were gained. It didn't mean that this new card would be 50% faster than the previous gen on all games. Why not using a latest gen PC, i.e., a Ryzen 7000 series CPU, an AM5 motherboard and DDR5 RAM modules, especially when AMD suggested that combining the Zen4 and RDNA3 architectures would bring extra benefits?

For me, the +20% price difference between this card and the RTX 4080 is relevant. It basically places them on different tiers and even then, the AMD card beats the NVIDIA one on most games in rasterization performance. If you want to play on the highest quality settings, RT included, be prepared to pay the price and don't complain. Even AMD has been open to admit that they're not on par when RT is enabled. And don't forget that some people spent $2000 for a 3090Ti not just long ago: AMD not only matched but exceeded the performance with this card, which is half the price.

Last, you forgot to mention that AMD video cards usually improve in time, they age much better than the NVIDIA cards. The 7900 XTX has 50% more memory than the RTX 4080. Today games probably don't make use of the 24 GB of RAM the 7900 XTX is equipped with but in the next few years, 16 GB won't be enough and performance on the NVIDIA card will be severely affected, allowing the AMD card to extend the overall rasterization difference and probably catching up in the RT department. FSR 3.0 is also around the corner, which will boost the RDNA3 GPUs even further. People who are considering buying this card or the RTX 4080 really need to consider this topic. I recently came across a video that analyzed a very similar situation between two video cards from 2013, the AMD R9 290X (MSRP $549) and an NVIDIA GTX 780Ti (MSRP $699), both released within 15-30 days (October 24th and November 7th, 2013), how they performed at launch, how did the drivers improve, how the memory difference impacted performance over the years, etc. I highly recommend watching it if really considering buying a new GPU: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBKKR4swcEE

Edit: One more thing, I promise: Capping to 90 fps to measure power efficiency? Really? Who spends more than $1000 in a video card to cap its performance? You forgot to mention that if you're upgrading your computer with the NVIDIA RTX 4090 (probably it applies to the 4080 too) , most likely you'll be required to buy a new power supply because it's much power hungry, even if it's more efficient FPS/Watt, plus a new case to actually make it fit inside the box.

comments.text:
Saw someone wondering if driver improvements might favor the 7900 XTX.

I mean, probably, AMD has a track record and there are some obvious unfavorable outliers. HOWEVER, AMD is a giant in its own right now and their "as the underdog we can't get our drivers together until 6 months after launch" schtick is losing its charm. Intel didn't really get a second chance with the public after the Arc driver situation (rightfully, IMO). I don't really think consumers should be extending much benefit of the doubt to AMD, given their position and resources.

At this point, underperforming on Day 1 is a choice that AMD is making. And that choice is bad for consumers. You only get one launch day, and AMD knows that's when most consumer sale decisions are going to be made. I think consumers should use the best information they have at the time their making their purchase decisions to avoid being taken advantage of. Plus, if you're going to just assume driver improvements will improve performance, you can't really assume Nvidia will stand still. Historically Nvidia improves less after day 1, but they do still improve, and that eats away at AMDs potential to change the overall story.

I guess, if I thought this would be a major factor in my decision, I would wait until I actually saw those issues dragging the 7900XTX's averages down resolved. I wouldn't lay my money on the line trusting AMD to eventually fix it. Particularly at this price point. Broadly speaking, if a product doesn't provide the value that you think it should, the best choice is to not buy it until that changes.

I think Linus did a much better real-world test of 8K gaming a few weeks ago, rendering at a lower resolution (4K if I recall) and upscaling to 8K which is much more realistic for modern hardware. I think that is a home run for AMD given the pricing situation as of now.  Of course we'll need to wait and see if the board partners follow similar pricing when they release their own cards... but I can't help thinking of all those people who spent their hard-earned money on the RTX 3090 during the chip shortage, and even now up to a few months ago after prices stabilized.  Now, new hardware exists that shows just how much of a waste the previous generation of GPUs really was.

The Radeon RX 6950 XT has seen its price drop by about $300 since its release 7 months ago, so who knows where final pricing on these newer cards will fall given time  From what I've seen with this generation of cards being bottlenecked by the CPU, I think we're at a point in this cycle where your choice of CPU is going to be more important than the choice of GPU if you want to really take advantage of the best performance available.

comments.text:
The 7900 XTX seems to be performing quite well relative to the RTX 4080. Now, I'll admit that doing well against a 4080 is a pretty low bar, but the 4080 is the 7900 XTX's main competition, and at $1000 USD, it's definitely compelling against the 4080 at 1200 USD. I actually don't think that the extra 200 is no big deal for a lot of people buying these cards. A lot of people who are going to be buying these cards are just gamers who care enough about gaming to pay a large chunk of their annual disposable income on a graphics card every 2-3 years. They're willing to get something if the price to performance makes sense. With the 4080, the price vs. performance just doesn't make as much sense. I can see people who start by looking at maybe buying an RTX 3080 or RX 6900 XT might see that going up to 1000 USD actually makes sense for them, whereas going up to 1200 for a 4080 won't make as much sense for them. 

There's also the "new" factor to consider. It's a newer architecture, and likely has more room to mature/ grow in performance vs. the 6000 series. Engine limitations, cpu bottlenecks, and a lack of driver optimization are all likely factors in holding these new cards back in a lot of these games (RTX 4000 series and RX 7000 series alike). Whether or not, and to what extent these cards are going to get better over time remains to be seen, but there certainly is a perception that newer is better. You're at least getting better power efficiency over previous gen cards, which is something.

Personally, 1000 USD is still out of my price range, and I also don't really feel that I need that much additional performance. I only recently upgraded to a 3080 anyway (got a good deal on it used).

comments.text:
Pretty sure AMD prefered stability for the reviews .. as the march-driver will require new benchmarks with hyper RX and hopefully FSR3. So i expect the coming drivers to bring a lot of performance in titels which underperform on the rx7900xt(x) currently. Still al numbers AMD stated were  "up-to" figures, and AMD optimized games and engines are still underway as devs are still working on console & pc versions/ports .. because of market share & developer-support games are optimised mostly for last gen NV hardware.. The RX7900 series might just tip that scale, and looking at CoD:MW2 results (even as an best-case scenario) that could hit hard.. 
You can use RT on AMD, which would get crazy performance increase vs the now standard RTX-like pipeline. Though that usage is totally incompatible with RTX. 
(RTX is an post-processing effect, and AMD-RT is more universal and broad applicable. Though implementing RT as an post-effect hurts RDNA#-RT accelerators, there is a bigger factor in the lookupstructure implementation on both uArch's .. AMD is wicked fast with object lookups and NV has mad skills at intersection-checking.
No dev gets budget to code a optimal path for RDNA for the PC port with 70%+ NV-share dGPU's. Most publishers will go: "Let AMD fix  it, or let them give us support".

That could change with consoles and pc sharing similar architecture, and support improving. Marketshare grows and so the need for a gamedev to optimize for a target GPU.

I always suspected that Nvidia priced the 4080 at $1,200 SPECIFICALLY to help retailers clear out all the leftover 30-series inventory that they had in stock.  Since 4080s are sitting on shelves all over the place, Nvidia will obviously lower the price in the near future...it just remains to be seen how much.  At $1,000, I would still go with the 4080 over AMD even though the 7900XTX may be SLIGHTLY faster at 4K, because Nvidia is dramatically ahead in raytracing performance AND their drivers are just miles and miles ahead of AMD graphics drivers.

But at $900?  At an $899 MSRP, Nvidia could potentially knock AMD out of the graphics game altogether.  Okay, that is probably an exaggeration...but not by much.  AMD has like 18% of the discreet graphics market while Nvidia has 82%.  You make the 4080 a $900 card and there is LITERALLY NO REASON AT ALL to buy an AMD 7900XT or XTX over a 4080.  NONE!

I am still waiting on 4090s to be more readily available to replace my 3090, so I don't really care either way about the 4080 or AMD's cards, but I will be interested to see if Nvidia is smart enough to take this opportunity while it exists, or if Jensen would rather just milk gamers for every penny he possibly can without worrying about Nvidia's market share.  As I said before...the 4080s at $900 would be a total no-brainer.  Only a true fanboy clown would buy an AMD 7900XTX or the weaker 7900XT over a 4080 at $900.  But even at $1,000, the Nvidia card is the better choice...it's just that at that price point, I could see SOME argument for going with the 7900XTX over the 4080.

comments.text: Your black screen issue sounds a whole lot like a black screen issue I've been having lately with my Samsung Neo G8. Apparently there's a huge bug with DSC (display stream compression) when overloaded with data such as in a situation where you are running the monitor (Neo G8) at it's native spec of 4K 240hz with G-Sync and HDR enabled. This is seemingly too much for DSC in its current form and it will cause your game to black screen or flicker on a loop. Some people have run into this issue when using multi monitor setups like 2 1440p 240hz monitors both using G-Sync or HDR. Whenever DSC is engaged to handle the data load, this issue is possible. I was extremely upset when I heard the 40 series were not supporting Display port 2.1 because that would've meant that 4K 240hz would have been possible without the compression. Nvidia is really so annoying, and AMD not impressive enough in performance and also the consistency of the performance in this video was all over the place. Fuck Nvidia though fr.

comments.text:
Some of these results make no sense, like the single digit percentage gains over the 6950XT. This indicates a serious driver issue on these cards, and as a buyer I cannot judge them based on future improvements. If I'm in the market for a $1000+ GPU I would want the best within reason, and the 7900XTX isn't it; The 4080 seems like a much more reasonable buy right now. If I'm shopping for a high end GPU but for less than $1000 then the 6800XT is the best bang for buck right now for $550, and maybe the $6900XT for $700. 

At a $1000 a few hundred more for a similar but more consistent performing card with far superior RT performance is an easy pill to swallow. Even the unlaunched and now renamed 4070Ti is a better buy than the 7900XTX at $900 for slightly less raster and still superior RT performance. RT has now gotten good enough where we should really start taking it seriously, unlike the unusable mess we've had with the RTX2000 and RX6000 series. 

AMD needs to either slash the price by another couple hundred dollars or improve their performance by massive margins overnight with driver updates, though I wouldn't hold my breath on it. At a $1000 they're just another sku that sits between the 4070Ti and the 4080 with no real incentive to go for it. Nvidia might as well make a $1000 sku themselves and kill the 7900XTX off completely.

comments.text:
Since when is performance not the most important feature in GPU's for gaming? We have about 5-10% faster performance than the RTX 4080 at $200 less and that is somehow not important enough? 

DLSS is nothing more than a gimmick to which AMD have their own gimmick that performs at 95 to 100% the rate DLSS does. You might say Nvidia's gimmick in some cases is 5% better overall, but that is almost nothing. Even ray tracing is a complete and utter gimmick right now and still will be 3 years in the future! We do not have GPU and won't have GPU's that are powerful enough to do actual real time ray tracing in the near future!

That is why it's now path tracing and shortcuts and gimmicks in RT, because REAL RT cannot be done and won't be able to be done for at least another 5 years! I said this when the RTX 2000 were released, find all of my comments, I wrote at least 20 times on this channel how RT is a gimmick and will be a gimmick for at LEAST 5 more years. Since then, it's been close to 5 years and I was right in that RT is still a gimmick. 

If you actually do hardcore type RT like in Portal you get 30fps even with an RTX 4090 and even that is not 100% real ray tracing. 

AMD has also introduced a new media engine in their 7000 series and I'm expecting it to be on par with Nvidia's media engine, since it pretty much uses the same codecs and techniques that Nvidia has been using! 

If you do want the best performance and have money to burn then I can see why someone would go for the RTX 4090, its the best money can buy and has no competition, but when we are talking any semblance of value or normalcy then the 7900XTX makes a lot of sense! Sure I would prefer it if it was cheaper, but I can say the same things about all products in the past several years! Realistically the RTX 4090 should be the $1000 Titan type GPU, with the high end 4080 and 7900xtx sitting at $650.
